description:
Prototype the 'build for architecture' side of the choice so the API decision has something concrete.

- A build option selecting the target: portable (today, default) or an architecture level (native, or a named level such as x86-64-v3, armv8.2-a+crc). Try more than one spelling: config :defk, target: ...; use Defk, target: ...; DEFK_TARGET env var for CI. Note what each feels like in a real mix.exs/config and in a Mix.install script.
- The target goes into the build cache key and the .so name (Defk.Build.cache_key/2).
- The .so records the features it was built with; on load it checks the running CPU (cpuid / getauxval / sysctl) and fails with a clear error naming the missing features and how to rebuild (portable), instead of SIGILL. Prototype the fallback alternative too (also build portable, load it on mismatch) and compare.
- Measure on real x86-64 and arm64 hardware with the research ticket's kernels: speedup per level, build time, .so size.
- Benchmark reporting: DEFK_RESULT and Defk.Bench.report include the target, so no example silently compares an architecture build.

Done when the prototype branch builds and loads both ways, the mismatch path is demonstrated (e.g. a v3 build loaded under an emulated older CPU), and the numbers are in docs/research/simd.md.
title: Prototype: opt-in architecture build with a load-time CPU check
